text:
rebekah: dropping a new pattern idea for the compare table: a tiny non-intrusive "pulse" indicator to show a row has metric history available. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/pulse-indicator
noah: Interesting. How does pulse differ from the micro-affordance we've used? My concern is motion and discoverability.
sumi: Pulse idea: static small dot that gently pulses on first load only to indicate presence, then becomes static. That balances discoverability without constant motion.
carl: Accessibility-first: any pulsing motion must respect prefers-reduced-motion. Also small dots need a focusable 44px hit target even if visually minimal. Use aria-hidden=false element for keyboard.
rebekah: Agreed. Implementation sketch: show pulse for 3 seconds after page load, then switch to static state. On keyboard focus the affordance expands to include text 'Inspect metrics' and role="button" with aria-controls to the inspector panel.
noah: Copy callout: 'Inspect metrics' vs 'View metrics' vs 'Open insights'. I think 'Inspect metrics' tells power users there's detailed history. Others prefer 'View metrics' for clarity.
sumi: I'm leaning 'Inspect metrics' for the compact table and 'View metrics' in the side panel header. Keeps in-row action more of a tool-like verb.
carl: Perf note: render a single SVG pulse element per visible row and reuse nodes for virtualization. Avoid per-row JS timers; drive pulse state from a single coordinator that marks rows as "seen".
aria-bot: Accessibility checklist: respects prefers-reduced-motion, 44px focusable target, contrast >=4.5:1 for any tiny text, aria-controls / aria-expanded for the inspector, announce state changes via aria-live.
rebekah: Nice checklist. Also: pinning UX question. If a user pins a version via the inspector, should the pulse indicator be suppressed for that version? We don't want pinned rows still pulsing.
sumi: Suppress pulse once pinned and add a subtle persistent pin stripe. Suggest microcopy: toast 'Pinned version saved to your view.' and aria-live announcement.
carl: Technical: pin state should be client-visible immediately (optimistic UI) then reconciled with server. API shape: POST /api/v1/pins {modelId, versionId, scope: 'user'|'team'}. Team scope requires admin perms.
noah: Filter persistence: users asked for filters to survive view switches. Proposed: encode filters into URL + store last-used filters per-user as fallback. Add a 'Save filter preset' CTA for shareable contexts.
sumi: UI: small saved-presets pill next to the search with a dropdown. When a preset is active, suppress pulses for rows that are excluded by the preset to avoid confusion.
rebekah: Badge ordering: suggest default order: latency, error rate, cost. But add a quick 'priority' dropdown on the badge tray to let users reorder. Keyboard accessible: up/down controls and numeric ordering.
aria-bot: A11y note: badge text at 11px requires high contrast. If badges show numeric metrics, include sr-only labels like 'Latency: 120 ms' and also ensure tooltips have accessible names.
carl: Motion details: pulse animation: scale from 0.9 -> 1.12 and fade opacity 0.8 -> 0.4 over 750ms. Use will-change: transform, opacity and force compositing for smooth GPU animation. But remove animations for prefers-reduced-motion.
noah: UX edge-case: paging or virtualization may re-trigger pulse when rows remount. Use a 'seen' cookie/localStorage keyed to model-version to avoid repeating pulse per session.
sumi: Good point. Also ensure that screen reader users get an announcement for new content: aria-live polite text 'Metrics available for version 2.1'. But don't spam.
rebekah: Action items: 1) I'll update figma with pulse timing + focus-expansion behavior, 2) add copy variants 'Inspect metrics' (row) + 'View metrics' (panel), 3) include aria strings + contrast tokens in the spec, 4) add pin API stub and optimistic UI notes, 5) add saved-filter preset UI. Will post staging link and PR tomorrow morning.
aria-bot: Accessibility walkthrough scheduled 2026-04-05 10:00 PT. RSVP required. Checklist attached: https://intranet.redwood.ai/a11y/pulse-pattern
noah: Quick dev ask: can we also include a small experiment flag to A/B pulse vs micro-affordance so we can measure engagement? If yes, I'll wire telemetry events.
sumi: +1 on experiment. Event names: catalog.row.pulse_shown, catalog.row.pulse_clicked, catalog.row.pulse_suppressed_pin.
rebekah: Excellent. Thanks team 20; I'll follow up with the figma and staging preview."
